reason: The text demonstrates that Yahweh does have empathy for the people. While Yahweh initially expresses severe anger at the people's idolatry and even declares intent to destroy them (וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה ... וַאֲכַלֵּם), Moses intercedes on behalf of the people, appealing to God's covenants and reputation. Critically, the text explicitly states that Yahweh relented from the evil he had spoken against the people (וַיִּנָּחֶם יְהוָה עַל־הָרָעָה אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לַעֲשׂוֹת לְעַמּוֹ). This relenting demonstrates divine compassion and empathy for the people despite their grave sin. While Yahweh does offer to make Moses into a great nation, this does not negate his ultimate mercy toward the people as a whole. The narrative structure shows empathy overriding wrath through the intercession mechanism.
